findings.claim: The analysis gives contradictory sycophancy-gate placement guidance, so a downstream plan could wire the enforced gate in the wrong place.
findings.evidence: Section 6a says: "validate-skill.sh is the enforced gate" and "Creators invoke validate-skill.sh. They do not call check-findings-sycophancy.sh directly." But Section 7 answers the assess open question #5 with the opposite: "Creator calls the existing check-findings-sycophancy.sh... Do not duplicate the logic inside validate-skill.sh." This also conflicts with the phase goal: "Promote the sycophancy pass ... to an enforced gate in validate-skill.sh."
findings.suggested_fix: Update Section 7 question #5 to match Section 6a: validate-skill.sh shells out to check-findings-sycophancy.sh as the single enforcement point, and creators call validate-skill.sh only.

findings.claim: The recommendation to add an MCP server surface to native-agent does not evaluate which existing Rust MCP server implementation should be reused or standardized.
findings.evidence: Section 1 notes multiple in-repo MCP/Rust assets: "rmcp versions: prometheus-research and sovereign-sync at 1.8, liter-llm at 2.1; substrate/sovereign-sync/src/mcp_server.rs exists — we already run a Rust MCP server." Section 9 then recommends: "Add an MCP server surface to native-agent," but gives no verdict on whether to reuse sovereign-sync's server, standardize on rmcp 2.1, support 1.8 compatibility, or create a new crate.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit build-vs-reuse decision for the MCP server surface: preferred rmcp version, whether sovereign-sync/src/mcp_server.rs is the reference implementation, and what compatibility or migration work is required.
